notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha 26 Released (The Performance Update)
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, airport CEO![/h1]

From the heart of GDC (Game Developers Conference) 2018, Alpha 26, [b]the performance update[/b], has finally made it to the default branch after months of development on the experimental branch. It addresses one of the core current issues of Airport CEO: Tanking FPS when you build larger airports and process larger amounts of persons. By overhauling several large systems from agent movement and agent path finding to optimizing data structures and rendering, we’ve managed to gain several frames per second by mitigating the top most crucial performance impact sources.

What we’ve been doing exactly can be seen in the patch notes below but do note that this is not really [i]the[/i] performance update, but [i]the first performance[/i] update. We have a lot more performance updates planned such as various additional data structure and micro optimizations to do including getting rid of certain minor spikes, solving the UI performance leaks, solving very specific bugs where a certain simulation situations can cause otherwise low impact code to be invoked excessively as well as experimenting with more efficient multi-threading solutions and new and experimental architectures that could massively boost the game engine’s ability to handle large amounts of moving agents (more on this in Monday’s development blog).

As with every default deployment, do expect hot-fixes to be deployed accordingly with the severity and frequency of filed bug reports. We will make sure to see that Alpha 26 is as stable as possible before we continue work on Alpha 27 on the experimental branch, and what will become then new UI. Parallel with working on the new UI we’ll make sure to again start including some new content and new features, what those will be will be disclosed in the devlogs as we deploy them on the experimental branch.

Here are the patch notes for Alpha 26:

notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha 25.0 Released
notes.notes:
[b]Hey there, airport CEO![/b]

The Alpha 25 version has now finally made its way to the default branch and that means a few big changes. The following text will briefly go through these but if you just want to see the patch notes they will be posted just below the following text segment.

Also, keep a lookout for DevLog 100 dropping in a few minutes after this is being posted. As mentioned in that DevLog you can expect hotfixes to be released for the default branch already tomorrow.

[b]New Flight Contract System[/b]

We can finally present the first version of the new airline contract system! The system is intended to improve the scheduling process and shift focus from tedious signing of new contracts to instead manage relationship with airlines.

Due to many changes under the hood your old contracts will be removed and all, except your active flights will be cancelled. This is a technically motivated and required effort to avoid breaking any ongoing turnarounds and keep old save integrity. These flights will however lose all connections to its airline and route which means that you will be presented with question marks ("?") or missing data for these flights when viewed in the UI. Please ignore this as any new flights will have the correct data. Simply let the old flights run through and your save should be fine (unfortunately these old flights will give you $0 income, it is not a bug just an effect of these changes).

[b]Contract Flow[/b]

You will now sign a master contract with an airline instead, which will (at least for now) not expire. The airline will then offer you flights (both single and reoccurring) depending on their current satisfaction of your airport. If you manage to get the flight away on time, the airline satisfaction will increase and vice versa if a flight is too delayed (you have a grace period of 1 hour, any more and your rating will be negatively impacted). More triggers for satisfaction will be added later on as the system be refined during its time on the experimental branch, based on your input.

[b]Auto Scheduler[/b]

For the really laid back CEOs we have now implemented an auto scheduling system which will schedule any new flights completely automatic at the next available slot. Just make sure you have both a COO and a CIO at your board to enable the toggle in the flight planner.

The auto scheduling system depends on an artificial intelligence bot named Asio and is constructed with a neural network utilizing machine learning and deep web analytics to plan your flights as best as they can be planned. Naaaaaah, just kidding, it’s just a set of if rules…

[b]Aircraft Ratio Slider[/b]

You will now be able to set the ratio of new flights to better control the offered flights suited for your airport layout. You will be able to modify the ratio of small, medium and large aircraft sizes (not that large flights do not exist yet, but this is to prepare for future implementations). For example, if you set the slider to 60% small and 40% medium, airlines will offer you randomized flights with sizes corresponding to these ratios.

[b]Individual Flight Ratings[/b]

Each flight now has a rating from one to five which is represented as stars similar to the contract system. Higher rated flights will earn you more money and for now you can get up to 3-star flights should all requirements be met. The airline will look at your facilities and offer flights rated at that level. If you click on the large star in the flight planner you can find out what you need to construct or offer to get higher rated flights. This feature is still experimental and we plan to add more requirements later when we have gathered some initial feedback from you all.

That’s it for the airline contract system, there are a few more sliders and control options implemented into the flight planner as of Alpha 25.0, however we have one more important things to mention.

[b]Massive Memory Leak Patched[/b]

Several of you have noticed that over time, when running an empty airport or an airport with a consistent passenger flow, the game has over time become sluggish and unplayable. We have now found, and patched, that issue which was related to an ancient code segment located in the security checkpoint class controlling the lights and effects (not kidding… in big projects like this code quickly becomes legacy). This issue is not immediately related to the number of passengers in your airport, for example running an airport with a few thousand passengers will still strain your CPU and is something we’re working on in another ticket, but at least the game will now stop killing your computer over time for no reason.

Speaking of performance, there’s now also a passenger ratio per flight slider accessible via the game panel (in game menu). Want to run more flights with less passengers? Use the slider to get the desired effect.

notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha 25.0 Released
notes.notes:
[b]Hey there, airport CEO![/b]

The Alpha 25 version has now finally made its way to the default branch and that means a few big changes. The following text will briefly go through these but if you just want to see the patch notes they will be posted just below the following text segment.

Also, keep a lookout for DevLog 100 dropping in a few minutes after this is being posted. As mentioned in that DevLog you can expect hotfixes to be released for the default branch already tomorrow.

[b]New Flight Contract System[/b]

We can finally present the first version of the new airline contract system! The system is intended to improve the scheduling process and shift focus from tedious signing of new contracts to instead manage relationship with airlines.

Due to many changes under the hood your old contracts will be removed and all, except your active flights will be cancelled. This is a technically motivated and required effort to avoid breaking any ongoing turnarounds and keep old save integrity. These flights will however lose all connections to its airline and route which means that you will be presented with question marks ("?") or missing data for these flights when viewed in the UI. Please ignore this as any new flights will have the correct data. Simply let the old flights run through and your save should be fine (unfortunately these old flights will give you $0 income, it is not a bug just an effect of these changes).

[b]Contract Flow[/b]

You will now sign a master contract with an airline instead, which will (at least for now) not expire. The airline will then offer you flights (both single and reoccurring) depending on their current satisfaction of your airport. If you manage to get the flight away on time, the airline satisfaction will increase and vice versa if a flight is too delayed (you have a grace period of 1 hour, any more and your rating will be negatively impacted). More triggers for satisfaction will be added later on as the system be refined during its time on the experimental branch, based on your input.

[b]Auto Scheduler[/b]

For the really laid back CEOs we have now implemented an auto scheduling system which will schedule any new flights completely automatic at the next available slot. Just make sure you have both a COO and a CIO at your board to enable the toggle in the flight planner.

The auto scheduling system depends on an artificial intelligence bot named Asio and is constructed with a neural network utilizing machine learning and deep web analytics to plan your flights as best as they can be planned. Naaaaaah, just kidding, it’s just a set of if rules…

[b]Aircraft Ratio Slider[/b]

You will now be able to set the ratio of new flights to better control the offered flights suited for your airport layout. You will be able to modify the ratio of small, medium and large aircraft sizes (not that large flights do not exist yet, but this is to prepare for future implementations). For example, if you set the slider to 60% small and 40% medium, airlines will offer you randomized flights with sizes corresponding to these ratios.

[b]Individual Flight Ratings[/b]

Each flight now has a rating from one to five which is represented as stars similar to the contract system. Higher rated flights will earn you more money and for now you can get up to 3-star flights should all requirements be met. The airline will look at your facilities and offer flights rated at that level. If you click on the large star in the flight planner you can find out what you need to construct or offer to get higher rated flights. This feature is still experimental and we plan to add more requirements later when we have gathered some initial feedback from you all.

That’s it for the airline contract system, there are a few more sliders and control options implemented into the flight planner as of Alpha 25.0, however we have one more important things to mention.

[b]Massive Memory Leak Patched[/b]

Several of you have noticed that over time, when running an empty airport or an airport with a consistent passenger flow, the game has over time become sluggish and unplayable. We have now found, and patched, that issue which was related to an ancient code segment located in the security checkpoint class controlling the lights and effects (not kidding… in big projects like this code quickly becomes legacy). This issue is not immediately related to the number of passengers in your airport, for example running an airport with a few thousand passengers will still strain your CPU and is something we’re working on in another ticket, but at least the game will now stop killing your computer over time for no reason.

Speaking of performance, there’s now also a passenger ratio per flight slider accessible via the game panel (in game menu). Want to run more flights with less passengers? Use the slider to get the desired effect.

notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha 24.0 Released
notes.notes:
Happy holidays airport CEO!

Alpha 24 has now been deployed on the default branch and this is quite a big change. You can read more about it in tonight's development blog but in short Alpha 24 is centered around improving and bringing in new content. 

[b]Please take note of the following changes that are relevant for your current default builds:[/b]

[list][*]Airlines does not specify contract class (star rating) anymore! This is preparations for the new contract system that we will present below.

[*]Push back vehicle is now required for medium stand operation. Make sure you purchase enough push back trucks for your airport.

[*]With the implementation of many new furniture and an updated variations system, both plants and gate seating will load as the default object (single row gate seating and small plant). The solution is to rebuild the object and save the world to store the correct variation.

[list]
[*]Runway operation has been updated and the following changes are required by players on the default branch. You might see aircraft warning that they cannot find a runway so it important to check below list:

[*]The desired allowed aircraft types must be set in the runway panel. Once this is set, save the game to store your settings.
    
[*]Medium aircraft now require either asphalt or concrete runway foundation to land/take-off.
    
[*]Medium aircraft now require at least 800 meters (or 2625 feet) of runway length.
[/list]
[/list]

We will be watching your incoming reports and will try to assist you with any stability issues that this change might bring. Please be advised that hotfixes for the default branch may arrive as we get incoming bug reports.

notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha 24.0 Released
notes.notes:
Happy holidays airport CEO!

Alpha 24 has now been deployed on the default branch and this is quite a big change. You can read more about it in tonight's development blog but in short Alpha 24 is centered around improving and bringing in new content. 

[b]Please take note of the following changes that are relevant for your current default builds:[/b]

[list][*]Airlines does not specify contract class (star rating) anymore! This is preparations for the new contract system that we will present below.

[*]Push back vehicle is now required for medium stand operation. Make sure you purchase enough push back trucks for your airport.

[*]With the implementation of many new furniture and an updated variations system, both plants and gate seating will load as the default object (single row gate seating and small plant). The solution is to rebuild the object and save the world to store the correct variation.

[list]
[*]Runway operation has been updated and the following changes are required by players on the default branch. You might see aircraft warning that they cannot find a runway so it important to check below list:

[*]The desired allowed aircraft types must be set in the runway panel. Once this is set, save the game to store your settings.
    
[*]Medium aircraft now require either asphalt or concrete runway foundation to land/take-off.
    
[*]Medium aircraft now require at least 800 meters (or 2625 feet) of runway length.
[/list]
[/list]

We will be watching your incoming reports and will try to assist you with any stability issues that this change might bring. Please be advised that hotfixes for the default branch may arrive as we get incoming bug reports.

Here's the complete change log and track record of the development Alpha 24 (with redundant per-experimental version update bug fixes).

notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha 23.1 Released
notes.notes:
Good evening (or day, or morning) airport CEO!

Since we with the deployment of Alpha 23 transitioned game engine and code framework version there were some imminent stability issues that needed immediate patching. Thus, Alpha 23.1 has after a few hours of soaking on the experimental branch been deployed on the default branch.

As we uncover and resolve more critical issues with this major version change (23.0) we might deploy additional revisions to the default branch (i.e. 23.2, 23.3 and so forth) but in general we will try to, as mentioned in DevLog 91, keep the minor iterations on the experimental branch and only deploy 24, 25 and so forth on the default branch.

Have a great weekend! Here are the patch notes for 23.1:

[h1]Release notes - Airport CEO - Version Alpha 23.1[/h1]
    
[b]        Improvement
[/b]
[list]
[*][url=https://apoapsisstudios.atlassian.net/browse/ACEO-2550]ACEO-2550[/url]] -         Implement sliders in favor of dropdowns on bathroom and runway panels
[/*]
[/list]
    
[b]        Bug
[/b]
[list]
[*][url=https://apoapsisstudios.atlassian.net/browse/ACEO-2469]ACEO-2469[/url]] -         Incorrectly built boarding desks can result in stuck passengers
[/*]
[*][url=https://apoapsisstudios.atlassian.net/browse/ACEO-2498]ACEO-2498[/url]] -         Persons serialized on Vector3.zero causes major loading lag freezing the applicationg
[/*]
[*][url=https://apoapsisstudios.atlassian.net/browse/ACEO-2503]ACEO-2503[/url]] -         Wierdly positioning of service truck causes baggage transition deadlock
[/*]
[*][url=https://apoapsisstudios.atlassian.net/browse/ACEO-2526]ACEO-2526[/url]] -         UI anchoring issue on game engine build version
[/*]
[/list]

notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha 23.0 Released
notes.notes:
Hello airport CEO!

It's been a while but finally Alpha 23.0 has made it to the default branch. You can learn more on why it's been delayed [url=https://www.airportceo.com/devlog-91-alpha-23-deployed-new-airline-design-contest/]in this week's devlog[/url] but for your convenience and excerpt of the development discussion will be included below:

[i]"A lot has happened under the hood, as the full patch notes can be seen here, and we've mainly targeted path finding performance improvements, general bug fixing and new UI feature implementation such as the long awaited employee job task overview sub panel and a vehicle stock overview panel.

The main reason for the delay has been stability concerns regarding the path finding system as we've been implementing new technology to improve performance. This initially brought a few critical bugs which we simply could not ship and took a few days of work to figure out and mitigate. Since a part of the solution to these bugs was to cycle the version of a key underlying component we had to do additional testing to the basic systems, one of which broke, before being confident in the stability of Alpha 23.

After soaking for a few hours on the experimental branch it has now been deployed and given its large changes we will continue to monitor its stability over the coming week. In the meantime we will split the remaining development time for this week in three halves, continued bug fixing where severity is prioritized, implementation of the new service vehicle pack and script profiling and optimization. When the ACEO development team is fully transitioned into their roles as professional game developers we will provide a set release schedule for the upcoming default branch deployments, most likely on a monthly basis but more information on this will be provided at a later stage."[/i]

[h1]New Versioning System[/h1]

We'd also like to highlight that we have a new and final versioning number system in place, here's a short summary:

[b]Airport CEO A B.C-D[/b]

[b]A:[/b] Major build type (incremented on major version transitions)
[b]B:[/b] Minor build version (incremented on larger and more stable changes to the code base (default branch))
[b]C:[/b] Revision number (incremented as new features and bug fixes are tested (experimental branch))
[b]D:[/b] Build version (incremented only when a new build is deployed on the experimental branch)

notes.title: Premature Evaluation: Airport CEO
notes.notes:
This week’s Premature Evaluation sees Fraser putting on his nicest suit and running an Airport in tycoon and management game Airport CEO [official site]. Please don’t arrange any flights until he’s finished. RPS does not endorse his airport.

I spend an inordinate amount of time in airports, and I loathe them with every fibre of my being. The huge crowds of people willing to sacrifice their humanity if it means getting on their flight in time; the constant, unrelenting announcements and security warnings; the forty different meaningless passenger classes; the endless, illogical queues — I m getting a stress headache just thinking about it.

So of course I ve decided to make my own airport in Airport CEO. I mean, how could anything I run be worse than one of these travel prisons? Frankly, I expect to do such a great job that I m wondering if this Premature Evaluation is even going to be interesting to read. Sorry.

notes.title: The Airport CEO Experimental Branch
notes.notes:
Good evening (Swedish time) everyone!

The Airport CEO Experimental Branch has now been made publicly available and is open for anyone to join in on to test the latest bug fixes and features of Airport CEO. But beware, the experimental branch might pack unsuspected bugs that have not been thoroughly tested!

The full message regarding the experimental branch can be viewed [url=https://forum.airportceo.com/t/the-airport-ceo-experimental-branch/4304]here[/url] but we have summarized the most important information below.

[list]
[*]The experimental branch will always feature a more un-stable version of Airport CEO.

[*]The experimental branch will always have a more recent version number than the default branch, except for when the experimental branch has been copied to the default branch.

[*]No public announcements will be done when the experimental branch is updated, except for when the first new experimental version is available after a default branch launch.
[/list]

We'd be happy to receive any input on these principles and workflow or if you have any other ideas or suggestions. Thank you for your continued support and we hope you'll enjoy testing out the experimental branch!

[i]Apoapsis Studios[/i]

notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha Version 0.22.0 Released
notes.notes:
Good evening (CEST) everyone!

0.22.0 is now released and brings a brand new tutorial (inspired by the community) and recurring flights! There's also several important bug fixes in place. Since the tutorial is new, there are some minor graphical adjustments that will be taken care of as we collect your feedback but the main focus will be understandability and how new players approach it. It is most likely still lacking some important information and bits but we think that this version at least has a proper chance of being perfected over time as opposed to the old one which was lacking in a few different aspects.

The tutorial overhaul has also acted as a bottle neck in our release pipeline which means that the faster, smaller releases have been put aside but we expect this to pick up again over the weekend as we get busy solving more issues. With this major overhaul finally out it also means that we can get back to putting effort into where it really matters, more bug fixing and being able to devote some time into looking at performance optimization and especially in the areas of memory leak bugs (we are aware of a few). 

Tomorrow we will post this week's devlog and discuss what's been going on and more interestingly the road ahead.

Since the tutorial is new, there are some minor graphical adjustments that will be taken care of as we collect your feedback but the main focus will be understandability and how new players approach it. It is most likely still lacking some important information and bits but we think that this version at least has a proper chance of being perfected over time as opposed to the old one which was lacking in a few different aspects.

The tutorial overhaul has also acted as a bottle neck in our release pipeline which means that the faster, smaller releases have been put aside but we expect this to pick up again over the weekend as we get busy solving more issues. With this major overhaul finally out it also means that we can get back to putting effort into where it really matters, more bug fixing and being able to devote some time into looking at performance optimization and especially in the areas of memory leak bugs (we are aware of a few). 

Tomorrow we will post this week's devlog and discuss what's been going on and more interestingly the road ahead.

notes.title: Devlog 89 delayed but here's a Short Update
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

Devlog 89 has been delayed in favor or working on important bug fixes and urgent feature implementations. However, it's been a few days since we last made talked so we just wanted to quickly bring you up to speed on what's going on.

We've made a short update post on the Forum and once 0.22.0 is deployed we will focus on writing a proper DevLog 89.

The update can be found by clicking [url=https://forum.airportceo.com/t/devlog-89-delayed-but-heres-a-short-update/4012]here[/url] but for your convenience we've pasted it below as well.

---------------

Hey everyone!

We’re delaying DevLog 89 due to wanting to put all time we have into bug fixing and testing. But we don’t wan’t to leave you in the dark so here is a short update for the previous week until alpha 0.22.0 has been deployed.

We’ve continued to investigate and solve issues related to stuck simulated agents (mostly aircraft and baggage) while also doing some notable overhauls to the tutorial as well as implementing recurring flights. Since these are major changes we’re leaving 0.21.x behind and are transitioning to 0.22.x to signal its significance and, also because it’s a major change, we wan’t to do some proper internal testing to try and mitigate any large scale issues forcing us to do a rollback as of what happened with 0.21.12. As soon as we have the proper organizational structure and the proper work methodologies we will enable everyone to join in on the experimental branch and by then we should also be able to make the Jira public.

[b]Here are some highlights for 0.22.0:[/b]

[list]
[*] Lacking path issue error handling for persons trying to access secure zone exits causing persons to walk through walls
[*] Issue with node connectivity on cargo bays (baggage bay) causing stuck baggage at check-in desks
[*] Issue with stuck bags at check-in desks
[*] Loans not properly serialized
[*] Enabled multiple announcement icons on object to better highlight accessibility issues (employees as well as service vehicles, bags will be added later)
[*] Stands do not merge with secure zone area upon build causing ramp agents not to find paths until after reload
[*] Recurring flights implemented
[*] New tutorial structure and features implemented
[/list]

If the final testing of recurring flights go well and when we’ve completed most of the tutorial overhaul we will deploy 0.22.0. We expect this to occur within the coming days.

In other news, the dev team is currently busy transitioning out of their current jobs to move into working with ACEO on a professional basis. We’d like to remind everyone that we are sadly, still, working with this on our free time which is why progression is not as swift as we want it to be. More information on this will follow as soon as we have more.

So that’s it for now, as I said when 0.22.0 is deployed we will focus on writing a proper devlog for edition 89. If you have any questions about anything we will happily answer them here!

---------------

Thanks and see you soon again!

notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha Version 0.21.12 Released
notes.notes:
Good evening, or maybe good morning, airport CEO!

As the globe keeps on turning we keep on churning out new patches. 0.21.11 patched a hole in the scheduling logic but in turn another was revealed causing a lot of flights to get randomly cancelled (honestly, we've all been at that airport...). notes.title: Airport CEO Alpha Version 0.21.11 Released
notes.notes:
Hej, airport CEO!

0.21.11 is now released and it packs a number of important fixes. Deadlocking mitigations on a few different fronts and new tech for rendering large areas with similar tiles. This is currently, for large scale testing purposes, limited to only include terminal foundation (and of course floor tiles) and stands. Moving ahead we will expand this to sidewalk and other smaller tiles as well (so large sidewalk areas will still cause some stress for your system) and also improve the system itself. This is a first step of many in bringing performance improvements and looking ahead we will focus on the mentioned improvements, LOD and of course night lights rendering.

notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

First off, we apologize for not posting the previous patch notes here but the last 24 hours has indeed been intense. We had a bit of a bumpy release with a small serialization issue that grew in proportion given the high sales in the beginning which was very unfortunate. We are still receiving a few bug reports on crashes and saves that do not load properly and all seem to be related to the first version issue, however we will thoroughly investigate all of these bugs.

We are also getting a few reports on game freezes and are looking into these as well trying to pinpoint hardware related issues. [b]If you are experiencing comprehensive issues with the game in terms of not being able to run it or in terms of resolution issues we urge you to return it so that you can get your money back.[/b]

notes.title: Airport CEO Bug Reporting
notes.notes:
[b]Airport CEO is about to be released to the public[/b] and that means that we will now be accepting public bug reports in an all community wide effort to improve the stability of ACEO these coming days and weeks.

We have set up an official inlet for bug reporting via the website. Go to https://www.airportceo.com/ and check the right side for a button that says “REPORT GAME BUG!”. Press it, follow the instructions and fill in the form. We will take it from there!

[olist]
    [*] Visit https://www.airportceo.com/

    [*] Press the “REPORT A GAME BUG!” button on the right side (you might have to empty your cache to see the button if you’ve recently visited the site)

    [*] Follow the instructions and submit your bug!
[/olist]

We of course realize that there is now way to control the discussion around bugs and that it will flow throughout the different channels but we do urge everyone who comes across a bug, [i]either if its minor or critical[/i], to report it via the main website.

[b]To get a better insight into the current missing features, know bugs of ACEO and troubleshooting, refer to this site:[/b]

https://www.airportceo.com/known-bugs-missing-features/

If there are any questions, suggestion or concerns we’d be happy to discuss them in this thread.

notes.title: Airport CEO Steam Store Page is now Live!
notes.notes:
[h1]A Word from the Developers[/h1]

[b]Hey there![/b] Glad to have you with us. [b]Airport CEO[/b] is a 2D tycoon and management game which has been in development for Windows and Mac since the summer of 2015. That's when we first announced what we were up to and two years later we are finally ready to let you try out and comment on what we've built so far.

Setting up this Steam store page is an important step towards the initial Early Access release of Airport CEO which we estimate to occur within August 2017. As we move closer to our internal release date, we'll make sure to share it with you. For more information on the exacts of the development process you can follow the Airport CEO development blog which is found over [url=https://www.airportceo.com/blog]here![/url] If you already have an opinion about the work we've done so far you are welcome to send us a comment on any of our various channels:

[list]
    [*] [url=https://forum.airportceo.com]The Airport CEO Forum[/url]
    [*] [url=https://www.twitter.com/airportceo]@AirportCEO on Twitter[/url]
    [*] [url=https://www.facebook.com/airportceo]Airport CEO on Facebook[/url]
    [*] [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/airportceo]The Airport CEO Subreddit[/url]
[/list]

We'll of course make sure to drop a message here when we release a new devlog, as well as any other content that might be relevant for you.

Thanks for stopping by and see you soon again!

[i]Apoapsis Studios[/i]
